key_insight: A single safety alignment effort can be propagated across many languages by enforcing consistency of model behavior across translations, enabling scalable multilingual safety without costly per-language supervision.
problem_solved: Reduces the need for large-scale, high-quality safety annotations or expensive pairwise alignments for each target language, addressing scalability and resource bottlenecks in multilingual LLM safety.
method: Use an English-aligned safety signal as the primary supervision source and propagate it to other languages via translated prompts/responses.
Enforce multilingual consistency constraints (e.g., consistency loss or agreement checks) so model outputs remain aligned across different language inputs.
Leverage lightweight, resource-efficient augmentation or regularization rather than full per-language reannotation or exhaustive pairwise alignment.
impact: Enables practitioners to achieve robust safety behaviors across many languages with far less annotation cost and engineering effort, making safer multilingual LLM deployment more practical and scalable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing single English alignment -> translation -> consistency enforcement -> multilingual model
Bar chart comparing annotation cost: per-language supervision vs. consistency-based propagation
Before/after examples: unsafe prompt in multiple languages with model responses showing improved aligned behavior
Icon set for scalability, cost, accuracy, and languages (globe with speech bubbles)
paper_title: Align Once, Benefit Multilingually: Enforcing Multilingual Consistency for LLM Safety Alignment
paper_authors: Yuyan Bu, Xiaohao Liu, ZhaoXing Ren, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai
